ἔχει οὖν ὧδε· οὐκ εἴ τι αἰώνιον ὁμωνύμως προσηγόρευται, θεὸς δύναται λέγεσθαι, ἀλλ' εἴ τις θεός, αἰωνίων ποιητής. γέγραπται γάρ· «χρόνων καὶ αἰώνων ποιητὴς ὁ θεός·» καὶ πάλιν· «Πολυμερῶς καὶ πολυτρόπως πάλαι ὁ θεὸς λαλήσας ἐν τοῖς προφή ταις, ἐπ' ἐσχάτου τῶν ἡμερῶν ἐλάλησεν ἡμῖν ἐν υἱῷ, ὃν ἔθετο κληρόνομον πάντων, δι' οὗ καὶ τοὺς αἰῶνας ἐποίησεν.» οὐ γὰρ εἴ τι αἰώνιον προσηγόρευται, θεὸς ὀφείλει ὀνομάζεσθαι· ἄπειροι θεοὶ ἔσονται. γέγραπται γάρ· «καὶ ἐπάρθητε, πύλαι αἰώνιοι,» καὶ πάλιν· «ἔτη αἰώνια ἐμνήσθησαν» καὶ αὖθις· «ὥσπερ πρόβατα αἰώνια,» καί· «ἀναστήσονται οὗτοι εἰς κόλασιν αἰώνιον.» καὶ ἑτέρωθι· «ἀναστήσονται οἱ ἐν χώματι γῆς, οἱ μὲν εἰς ζωὴν αἰώνιον, οἱ δὲ εἰς αἰσχύνην αἰώνιον.» ἆρα οὖν καὶ ἡ κόλασις καὶ ἡ αἰσχύνη θεοί; ὁρᾶς, εἰς ὅσην ἀτοπίαν καὶ ἀσέβειαν ἡ κατὰ τὸ αἰώνιον ὁμωνυμία ἐκπίπτει, τοῖς μὲν οὖν ἐκείνων νοήμασι καὶ ῥήμασιν ἅλμη ἐπιπολάζει τε καὶ συμπέφυρται· ταύτην δὲ διαλύει τάδε· τοῦ αἰωνίου ὀνόματος ὡς ἄρτι ἐπεμνήσθημεν, τὰ ἄλλα κἂν ἔτυχεν, μόνον οὐκ ἀπὸ χρόνου ἔτυχεν· ἀλλὰ καὶ φθορὰν τὴν ἀπὸ γνώμης οἰκείας τροπὴν ἔχει, καὶ ἀνόμοιον παντάπασιν τῷ θείῳ αἰωνίῳ τὸ ἐκείνων αἰώνιόν ἐστιν· καθὰ οὐδὲ ὁ λεγόμενος ἅγιος, ἄγγελος ἢ ἄνθρωπος, ὁμοίως καὶ ἴσως τοῦτό ἐστιν τῷ ἁγίῳ τῶν ἁγίων πνεύματι· αὐτὸ γὰρ ἁγιότης καὶ αἰωνιότης τὸ πᾶν ὑπάρχει. πρόσχωσι τοίνυν, μετὰ ποίας μεγαλοφωνίας τὸ αἰώνιον ἐπὶ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος ἀνείρηται, καὶ ὅτι τούτῳ τὸ θαυμαστὸν ἐκεῖνο καὶ πᾶσιν ἀχωρητότατον προσεπέθηκεν, φημὶ τὸ διὰ τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος τὸν κατασκευάσαντα τοὺς αἰῶνας ἑαυτὸν προσαγαγεῖν τῷ ἑαυτοῦ ἀληθινῷ πατρὶ ὑπὲρ ἡμῶν. σκεψάσθωσαν δὲ καὶ ὅτι αἱ δυνάμεις πᾶσαι τῶν οὐρανῶν ἐν τῷ ἁγίῳ πνεύματί εἰσιν, πάντως ὅτι ὡς συνδημιουργῶ τοῦ ἀνεπιδεοῦς δημιουργοῦ· καὶ ὅτι, ὧν οὐκ εὐκαίρως, ἀλλ' ἐνδιασκεύως ἐμνημόνευσαν αἱρετικοὶ αἰωνίων πυλῶν καὶ προβάτων, τὸ τέλος τὰ εἰς τὸ κεφάλαιον τοῦτο προκομισθέντα πρὸς ἡμῶν λόγια προεῖπαν. καὶ ἔστω δῆλον αὐτοῖς τὸ διάφορον τοῦ τε ἀνάρχως καὶ ἀτρέπτως αἰωνίου τοῦ τε ἀπὸ χρόνου καὶ τρεπτοῦ, καὶ ὡς οὐ βραχὺ τοῦτο, οὐδὲ περὶ τὴν οὐσίαν καὶ ἄλλο κάλλος ἐστὶ μόνον, ἀλλὰ τὸ παντάπασιν ἐξηλλαγμένον. ἔστω δὲ γνώριμον καὶ τὸ, ὅτι τὸ ἅγιον πνεῦμα τὴν περὶ τὸ αἰώνιον κρίσιν πρὸς τὸν ἐνισχύσαντα τὰ σύμπαντα θεὸν πατέρα καὶ τὸν υἱὸν ἔχει, οὐ πρὸς τὰ κτίσματα· καὶ λύσαντες τὴν χείρω γνώμην, ἑλέσθωσαν τὴν βελτίονα· καὶ θαυμαζέτωσαν, ἀντὶ τῶν νῦν, ἃ θαυμάζειν ἄξιον· καὶ πραξάτωσαν βελτίω τὸν μετὰ ταῦτα χρόνον· φθόνος γὰρ οὐδείς· καὶ ἀφ' ὧν τὴν ἀλαζόνα μέμψιν ποιησάμενοι ἑαυτοὺς ἔβλαψαν, ἐντεῦθεν καὶ τὸ τῆς μεταμελείας ὄφελος ἀπενεγκάσθωσαν. εἰ γάρ, ὡς θεοπρεπές τι ἐνδεικνυμένη ἡ λέξις αὕτη ἐχρήσθη περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ, ἴσως καὶ ὁμοίως ἐκληφθείη ἂν περὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ θεοῦ. ἓν μὲν δὴ τοῦτο· ἕτερον δέ, ὅτι οὐδὲν, ὧν ἐμνήσθησαν αἰωνίων, προσηγόρευται θεῖον, ἢ πνεῦμα ἅγιον ἐκ τοῦ θεοῦ ἐκπορευθέν, ἤγουν ἕν τι, καὶ μὴ πλῆθος ὄν· οὐδὲ συντάττεται τῷ πατρὶ καὶ τῷ υἱῷ εἰς θείαν μυσταγωγίαν καὶ θεϊκὴν δωρεάν, οὐδὲ ἄλλης τινός, ἵνα μὴ πολλὰ λέγω, θεότητι ἀνηκούσης τιμῆς ἠξίωται. ἄλλα πρὸς τούτοις· ὁ θεὸς καὶ πατὴρ εὐδόκησεν διὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγου πάντα δημιουργηθῆναι. καὶ ποία, ὡς ὀνειροπολοῦσιν, λοιδορία τῷ πνεύματι αὐτοῦ τῷ παναγίῳ ἐκ τοῦ μὴ δημιουργῆσαι, εἴ γε ἄρα, κατ' αὐτοὺς, μὴ ἀρρήτως συνεργόν ἐστι τῷ δημιουργῷ ὡς ὁ πατήρ; ὅτι δὲ τοῦ μονογενοῦς αὐτοῦ υἱοῦ λόγου καὶ τοῦ ἑνὸς ἁγίου πνεύματος πᾶσα ἐνέργεια καὶ δωρεά, δημιουργική τε, ἀγαθή τε καὶ τελεία, καὶ κοινὴ αὐτῶν ὑπάρχει, But it is not, it is not possible to hear with the ear the things which those set against the theologies of the Holy Spirit have laid down on this head too. For they lead themselves away to the ends of the earth from preconception; and undiscerning love (printed page 57 here) is not wont to bear witness to an exact examination; yet nothing, as it were, hinders hearing that very plausible contrivance; for so they would be condemned still more. It goes, then, thus: not if something has been addressed as eternal by a shared name can it be called God, but if someone is God, he is maker of eternal things. For it is written: 'God is maker of times and ages'; and again: 'in many parts and many ways of old God, having spoken in the prophets, at the last of the days spoke to us in a Son, whom he set as heir of all things, through whom he also made the ages.' For not if something has been addressed as eternal is it owed to be named God: there will be boundless gods. For it is written: 'and be lifted up, eternal gates', and again: 'eternal years were remembered', and again: 'like eternal sheep', and: 'these will rise into eternal punishment', and elsewhere: 'those in the dust of the earth will rise, some into eternal life, others into eternal shame.' Are then both the punishment and the shame gods? You see into how much out-of-placeness and impiety the sharing of name as to the eternal falls out. Now on their thoughts and words brine floats on top and has been mixed in; but these things dissolve it: of the name eternal, as we just now mentioned, the other things, even if they obtained it, not only (copy-text order: only not) obtained it from time; but also have corruption, the turning from their own judgement, and their eternal is altogether unlike the divine eternal; just as neither is one called holy, angel or human, this in like and equal manner with the Spirit, holy of the holies; for he is holiness and eternity the whole. Let them attend then with what loftiness of voice the eternal has been proclaimed of the Holy Spirit, and that to this he added that wonderful thing and most uncontainable by all, I mean the one who fashioned the ages having brought himself through the Holy Spirit to his own true Father on our behalf. And let them consider also that all the powers of the heavens are in the Holy Spirit, surely because as in a fellow-creator of the Creator who lacks nothing; and that, of the eternal gates and sheep which heretics mentioned not opportunely but for show, the oracles brought forward by us for this head foretold the end. And let the difference be plain to them between the eternal without beginning and without turning and the one from time and turnable, and that this is not short, nor is it only about the substance and another beauty, but the thing altogether made different. And let this also be known, that the Holy Spirit has the judgement concerning the eternal toward God the Father, who strengthened all things, and the Son, not toward the creatures; and loosing the worse opinion, let them choose the better; and let them wonder, instead of the present things, at what is worthy to wonder at; and let them fare better for the time after these things; for there is no grudging; and from the things over which, making the boastful blame, they harmed themselves, from there let them carry off the profit of repentance too. For if, as showing something befitting God, this word was used about God the Father and the Son, equally and alike it would be taken about the Spirit of God. One thing, then, is this; and another, that nothing of the eternal things they mentioned has been addressed as divine, or Holy Spirit proceeding out of God, that is, as one thing and not being a multitude; nor is it ranked with the Father and the Son into divine initiation and godly gift, nor, so that I do not say many things, has it been counted worthy of any other honour belonging to the Godhead. Other things besides these: the God and Father was well pleased that all things be created through his Son the Word. And what sort of reviling, as they dream, to his all-holy Spirit out of not having created, if indeed, according to them, he is not ineffably a co-worker with the Creator as the Father? But that every working and gift, both creative and good and perfect, both is of his only-begotten Son the Word and of the one Holy Spirit and is common to them, and all things are led up to the One, out of whom and with whom these blessed hypostases unspeakably shone forth, he would most easily learn who quietly made some examination of the oracles full of wisdom, both those recalled in various places of this book, and those in the one before it. pass_b_english: … today, the same for ever” (Hebrews 13:8). But what those who are hostile to the theology of the Holy Spirit have laid down on this head too cannot, simply cannot, be borne by the ear. For prejudice carries them off to the ends of the earth, and an undiscerning passion does not usually show the marks of careful examination. Still, nothing hinders us, so to speak, from hearing that very piece of plausible pleading; for in this way they would be condemned all the more.

It runs like this. If something has been called “eternal” by a shared name, it cannot for that reason be called God; rather, if anyone is God, he is the maker of eternal things. For it is written: “God is the maker of times and ages”; and again: “In many parts and in many ways God spoke of old in the prophets; in the last of the days he has spoken to us in a Son, whom he appointed heir of all things, through whom he also made the ages” (Hebrews 1:1-2). For if a thing has been called eternal, it is not bound to be named God; otherwise there will be countless gods. For it is written: “And be lifted up, eternal gates” (Psalm 24:7); and again: “Eternal years were remembered” (Psalm 77:5); and once more: “like eternal sheep”; and: “These will rise to eternal punishment” (Matthew 25:46); and elsewhere: “Those in the dust of the earth will rise, some to eternal life, and some to eternal shame” (Daniel 12:2). Are the punishment and the shame gods, then? You see into how much absurdity and impiety this sharing of the name “eternal” falls.

Now in their thoughts and words a brine floats on the surface and is mixed all through; but what follows dissolves it. As we mentioned just now, the other things, even if they did obtain the name “eternal”, not only obtained it from a point in time, but are also subject to corruption, the turning that comes from their own will; and their “eternal” is altogether unlike the divine eternal. In the same way, one who is called holy, whether angel or man, is not holy in like and equal measure with the Spirit, the holy of holies; for the Spirit is holiness and eternity entire.

Let them attend, then, to the grandeur of speech with which “eternal” has been proclaimed of the Holy Spirit, and to the fact that Paul added to it that wonderful thing, beyond the grasp of all: I mean that through the Holy Spirit the one who fashioned the ages offered himself to his own true Father on our behalf. Let them consider, too, that all the powers of the heavens are in the Holy Spirit, surely as in the fellow-creator of the Creator who needs nothing; and that the very oracles we brought forward on this head foretold the end of those eternal gates and sheep which the heretics mentioned, not to the point but for effect.

And let the difference be clear to them between what is eternal without beginning and without change, and what is eternal from a point in time and is changeable. Let it be clear that this difference is not small, nor does it lie only in the substance and in some further beauty: it is a difference in every respect. Let this too be known: the Holy Spirit, when called eternal, is to be judged alongside God the Father, who gave strength to all things, and alongside the Son, not alongside the creatures. So let them give up the worse opinion and choose the better. Instead of what they admire now, let them admire what is worth admiring, and let them fare better in the time to come; no one grudges it. And from the very points on which they hurt themselves by their boastful fault-finding, let them now carry off the profit of repentance.

For if this word was used of God the Father and of the Son as showing something worthy of God, it would be taken equally and in the same way of the Spirit of God. That is one point. Another is this: none of the “eternal” things they mentioned has been called divine, or Holy Spirit proceeding from God, or even a single being rather than a multitude. None is ranked with the Father and the Son in the divine initiation and the divine gift; nor, not to say more, has any been thought worthy of any other honour that belongs to the Godhead.

There are other points besides. God the Father was pleased that all things should be created through his Son, the Word. And what slur, as they dream, is it on his all-holy Spirit that he did not create, unless indeed, by their account, he is not ineffably a co-worker with the Creator, as the Father is? That every working and gift, creative, good and perfect, belongs to his only-begotten Son the Word and to the one Holy Spirit and is common to them, while all of it is referred back to the One from whom and with whom these blessed hypostases shone forth in a way past telling: this anyone would learn very easily who quietly examined the oracles full of wisdom, both those cited in various places of this book and those in the book before it. choices.issue: Old draft garbled, an argument reversed, wrong references
choices.choice: Retranslated the whole section from the Greek. The old English began with an invented heading 'Regarding the phrase unto the ages of ages' for the end of Hebrews 13:8, made the heretics' claim ('not everything called eternal is God') say the opposite, read καταγνωσθείησαν ('they would be condemned') as 'make it more widely known', ἀνεπιδεής ('needing nothing') as 'ungraspable', ἐνδιασκεύως as 'in confusion', πρόβατα as 'thresholds', τὴν κρίσιν πρός ('is judged alongside') as 'holds the eternal judgment toward', ἴσως ('equally') as 'perhaps', ὑποστάσεις as 'hypotheses' and ἀπελούσασθε ('you were washed') as 'you were removed'; it also broke a paragraph mid-sentence after 'and that,'. References fixed: 'Ps 90:2' given to the unplaced 'God is the maker of times and ages' (removed; see problems); Heb 1:1-2, Ps 24:7 and Matt 25:46 written out; Hebrews 13:8 added. Printed page numbers 57 and 58 omitted.

choices.english: … today, the same for ever” (Hebrews 13:8)
choices.why: The quotation began at the end of the previous section; only this section's words are translated, with a leading ellipsis, and the reference is given here where the quotation ends.

choices.term: οὐκ ἔστιν δέ, οὐκ ἔστιν ἀκοῇ ἀκοῦσαι
choices.english: cannot, simply cannot, be borne by the ear
choices.why: Didymus doubles οὐκ ἔστιν for emphasis; kept.

choices.english: an undiscerning passion
choices.why: 57 is a printed page number in the copy-text; page debris, omitted.

choices.english: It runs like this
choices.why: Introduces the heretics' plausible argument, which runs to 'falls' at the end of the paragraph; Didymus' answer begins with 'Now in their thoughts and words a brine floats'.

choices.english: “God is the maker of times and ages”
choices.why: Not found as a verse of Scripture; no reference given (the old 'Psalm 90:2' does not say it).

choices.english: “Eternal years were remembered” (Psalm 77:5)
choices.why: Greek Psalm 76:6 (English 77:5), where the Hebrew means 'the years of ancient times'; the copy-text has the passive plural for the Septuagint's 'I remembered'.

choices.english: “These will rise to eternal punishment” (Matthew 25:46)
choices.why: Matthew 25:46 reads 'will go away'; the heretics' quotation has 'will rise', perhaps from Daniel 12:2 which follows. Translated as given.

choices.term: τὰ ἄλλα κἂν ἔτυχεν, μόνον οὐκ ἀπὸ χρόνου ἔτυχεν· ἀλλὰ καὶ φθορὰν … ἔχει
choices.english: even if they did obtain the name “eternal”, not only obtained it from a point in time, but are also subject to corruption
choices.why: The copy-text's 'μόνον οὐκ' gives no sense before ἀλλὰ καί; read as 'οὐ μόνον … ἀλλὰ καί' ('not only … but also'), matching 'eternal from a point in time and changeable' below. See problems.

choices.english: the Spirit, the holy of holies
choices.why: Didymus applies the superlative 'holy of holies' to the Spirit.

choices.english: Paul added
choices.why: The verb has no expressed subject; the addition is Hebrews 9:14, quoted as Paul's in the previous section.

choices.term: πάντως ὅτι ὡς συνδημιουργῷ τοῦ ἀνεπιδεοῦς δημιουργοῦ
choices.english: surely as in the fellow-creator of the Creator who needs nothing
choices.why: ὡς with the dative resumes 'in the Holy Spirit'; ἀνεπιδεής means 'needing nothing' (the Creator does not need a helper, yet the Spirit creates with him).

choices.term: ὧν … αἰωνίων πυλῶν καὶ προβάτων, τὸ τέλος … προεῖπαν
choices.english: the very oracles we brought forward on this head foretold the end of those eternal gates and sheep
choices.why: The relative ὧν depends on τὸ τέλος; the oracles are those of the previous chapter ('heaven and earth will pass away', new heavens and new earth).

choices.term: οὐδὲ περὶ τὴν οὐσίαν καὶ ἄλλο κάλλος ἐστὶ μόνον
choices.english: nor does it lie only in the substance and in some further beauty
choices.why: Kept close to the Greek; the point is that the difference is total, not one of degree.

choices.term: τὴν περὶ τὸ αἰώνιον κρίσιν πρὸς … ἔχει
choices.english: when called eternal, is to be judged alongside
choices.why: κρίσιν ἔχειν πρός: to be assessed in comparison with; the Spirit's 'eternal' is measured by the Father's and the Son's, not by creatures'.

choices.english: equally and in the same way
choices.why: ἴσως here pairs with ὁμοίως ('equally'), not 'perhaps'.

choices.term: ἤγουν ἕν τι, καὶ μὴ πλῆθος ὄν
choices.english: or even a single being rather than a multitude
choices.why: The 'eternal' things cited are plural (gates, years, sheep); the Spirit is one.

choices.term: εἰς θείαν μυσταγωγίαν καὶ θεϊκὴν δωρεάν
choices.english: in the divine initiation and the divine gift
choices.why: Baptism into the Father, Son and Holy Spirit; listed as a possible allusion to Matthew 28:19.

choices.term: εἴ γε ἄρα, κατ' αὐτούς, μὴ ἀρρήτως συνεργόν ἐστι
choices.english: unless indeed, by their account, he is not ineffably a co-worker
choices.why: εἴ γε … μή read as 'unless indeed': the Father too creates through the Son and is no less for it; so the Spirit is slighted only if he is denied the Father's co-working.

choices.english: quietly
choices.why: Copy-text spelling of ἡσυχῇ.

choices.english: greater than human measure
choices.why: Literally 'greater than according to men'.

choices.english: “But you were washed, but you were justified, but …
choices.why: 1 Corinthians 6:11, continued in the next section, where the reference is given.
